cloze.title: 原文选词填空
cloze.instruction: 从词库中选择合适的词填入空白，每词使用一次，保留原文词形。大小写不影响判分。

parts.text:
The limits of concrete and steel

Many engineered assets were designed for a stable climate that no longer exists.

Coastal

designed to repel mid-20th century level storm surges are being breached with growing regularity.

As rainfall patterns shift, a rise in extreme rainfall can overwhelm drainage systems built for the last century. In 2022, severe summer downpours caused the

of water infrastructure in Jackson, Mississippi. This year, intense cloudbursts turned streets into raging rivers in Saitama, Japan.

Once built, concrete and steel do their job until they fail. But living systems can respond by adjusting to new patterns of

, rainfall and sediment deposition rather than simply failing.

The idea isn’t new. In the 1990s, New York City authorities spent roughly A$2.1 billion protecting forests and plants in the city’s watershed. As a result, they avoided the need to build a

filtration plant, which would have cost an estimated $8.6-11 billion.

Many other nations have embraced cheaper, more flexible green infrastructure.

Mangroves protect coastlines

Tropical nations face the worst risk from sea level rise, as they are home to more than 60% of the world’s

coastlines.

Even if greenhouse emissions are drastically reduced, by 2100 seas will rise about 0.6 metres above 2000 levels. If emissions don’t fall sharply, sea level rise will be more like 2.2m.

Without efforts to

, encroaching seas could do more than $27 trillion in damage globally.

Governments often build seawalls and dykes to protect coasts. These can work, but they cost a great deal and can fail catastrophically under extreme conditions.

By

, fast-growing mangroves naturally dampen storm surges and inundation. Protection from the world’s existing mangrove forests is worth an estimated A$1.2 trillion over 100 years.

Planting mangroves typically cost less than 50% of the cost of concrete and steel

for the same protection, while the value of avoided property damage can be 10 to 100 times greater than planting costs.

In the Mekong Delta, authorities are combining grey and green infrastructure, planting mangrove belts to give built

a longer lifespan and cut maintenance costs.

Forests are water infrastructure

It makes good financial sense to replant forests in city watersheds, as they naturally filter rainwater as it fills dams. Protecting
forests – and the watersheds they protect – is also sensible, as these act as vital water infrastructure, recycling water and even generating rainfall.

questions.evidence: Coastal defences designed to repel mid-20th century level storm surges are being breached with growing regularity.

questions.explanation: 原文此处使用 failure（failure）。结合上下文辨认词义与词形。
questions.evidence: In 2022, severe summer downpours caused the failure of water infrastructure in Jackson, Mississippi.

questions.evidence: Protecting intact forests – and the watersheds they protect – is also sensible, as these act as vital water infrastructure, recycling water and even generating rainfall.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Wildfire damage is likely to increase, but affordable protective measures can reduce future losses.
Both artificial and natural wetlands can provide important habitat for young turtles.
Natural ecosystems can provide climate adaptation at lower cost than many engineered structures.
Routine water-quality reports cover only part of what matters for understanding drinking water.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: Planting mangroves typically cost less than 50% of the cost of concrete and steel equivalents for the same protection, while the value of avoided property damage can be 10 to 100 times greater than planting costs.

questions.prompt: What advantage can living systems offer over grey infrastructure?
options: They can adapt as climate conditions change.
They are always unaffected by any environmental pressure.
They require steel reinforcement to remain alive.
They perform no protective function.
questions.explanation: 第 4 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: Unlike grey infrastructure of steel and concrete, these living systems can adapt as the climate shifts.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 15?
options: The default is to reach for concrete and steel to build seawalls, dykes, dams and drainage systems.
But these decisions often don’t weigh up green infrastructure fairly, because wider benefits such as avoided flood risks and water services aren’t typically included in the accounting framework used.
Even if greenhouse emissions are drastically reduced, by 2100 seas will rise about 0.6 metres above 2000 levels.
Mangroves, forests and urban trees can help protect humans and their homes, farms and cities from floods, droughts, rising seas and heat.
questions.explanation: 定位第 15 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: Even if greenhouse emissions are drastically reduced, by 2100 seas will rise about 0.6 metres above 2000 levels.
